sanskrit: tat prayātaṃ balaṃ ghoram aśivaṃ śoṇitodakam abhyavarṣan mahāmeghas tumulo gardabhāruṇaḥ
english: As that dreadful army, inauspicious as a river of blood, set out, a great roaring cloud, dark as a donkey's hide, rained down upon it.

sanskrit: nipetus turagās tasya rathayuktā mahājavāḥ same puṣpacite deśe rājamārge yadṛcchayā
english: His swift horses, yoked to the chariot, stumbled and fell on their own on the royal road in a flower-strewn level place.

sanskrit: śyāmaṃ rudhiraparyantaṃ babhūva pariveṣaṇam alātacakrapratimaṃ pratigṛhya divākaram
english: A dark halo edged with blood appeared, resembling a wheel of firebrands, encircling the sun.

sanskrit: tato dhvajam upāgamya hemadaṇḍaṃ samucchritam samākramya mahākāyas tasthau gṛdhraḥ sudāruṇaḥ
english: Then a huge and terrible vulture alighted on the tall golden-shafted standard, clutching and perching upon it.

sanskrit: janasthānasamīpe ca samākramya kharasvanāḥ visvarān vividhāṃś cakrur māṃsādā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ
english: Near Janasthāna, flesh-eating beasts and birds, braying with harsh voices, made various discordant cries.

sanskrit: vyājahruś ca padīptāyāṃ diśi vai bhairavasvanam aśivā yātu dāhānāṃ śivā ghorā mahāsvanāḥ
english: In the blazing quarter of the sky, dreadful jackals uttered terrifying, inauspicious howls, portending ill for the living.

sanskrit: prabhinnagirisaṃkāśās toyaśoṣitadhāriṇaḥ ākāśaṃ tad anākāśaṃ cakrur bhīmā balāhakāḥ
english: Fearsome storm-clouds, resembling cleaved mountains, carrying rain dried within, made the sky no sky—obscuring it utterly.

sanskrit: babhūva timiraṃ ghoram uddhataṃ romaharṣaṇam diśo vā vidiśo vāpi suvyaktaṃ na cakāśire
english: A terrible, oppressive darkness arose that made the hair stand on end; neither the cardinal directions nor the intermediate ones could be clearly discerned.

sanskrit: kṣatajārdrasavarṇābhā saṃdhyākālaṃ vinā babhau kharasyābhimukhaṃ nedus tadā ghorā mṛgāḥ khagāḥ
english: A glow the color of wet blood appeared though it was not twilight, and dreadful beasts and birds cried out facing toward Khara.

sanskrit: nityāśivakarā yuddhe śivā ghoranidarśanāḥ nedur balasyābhimukhaṃ jvālodgāribhir ānanaiḥ
english: Jackals, ever portending ill in battle, terrible in their appearance, howled before the army with mouths belching flames.

sanskrit: kabandhaḥ parighābhāso dṛśyate bhāskarāntike jagrāha sūryaṃ svarbhānur aparvaṇi mahāgrahaḥ
english: A headless torso (kabandha), resembling an iron bar, was seen near the sun; and the great planet Svarbhānu seized the sun though it was not an eclipse-node.

sanskrit: pravāti mārutaḥ śīghraṃ niṣprabho 'bhūd divākaraḥ utpetuś ca vinā rātriṃ tārāḥ khadyotasaprabhāḥ
english: A fierce wind blew; the sun became devoid of luster; and stars with the faint glow of fireflies rose though it was not night.

sanskrit: saṃlīnamīnavihagā nalinyaḥ puṣpapaṅkajāḥ tasmin kṣaṇe babhūvuś ca vinā puṣpaphalair drumāḥ
english: Lotus-pools saw their fish and birds withdraw and their lotuses close; and at that moment trees stood bare of flowers and fruit.

sanskrit: uddhūtaś ca vinā vātaṃ reṇur jaladharāruṇaḥ vīcīkūcīti vāśyanto babhūvus tatra sārikāḥ
english: Dust of a cloud-red hue was stirred up with no wind, and mynahs (sārikā) there called out in mournful, broken cries.

sanskrit: ulkāś cāpi sanirghoṣā nipetur ghoradarśanāḥ pracacāla mahī cāpi saśailavanakānanā
english: Fiery meteors fell with terrible sounds; and the earth itself trembled along with its mountains, forests, and groves.

sanskrit: kharasya ca rathasthasya nardamānasya dhīmataḥ prākampata bhujaḥ savyaḥ kharaś cāsyāvasajjata
english: Even as the wise Khara stood in his chariot roaring, his left arm trembled involuntarily, and his voice faltered.

sanskrit: sāsrā saṃpadyate dṛṣṭiḥ paśyamānasya sarvataḥ lalāṭe ca rujā jātā na ca mohān nyavartata
english: His gaze, looking all about, became tearful; a pain arose in his forehead; yet from delusion he did not turn back.

sanskrit: tān samīkṣya mahotpātān utthitān romaharṣaṇān abravīd rākṣasān sarvān prahasan sa kharas tadā
english: Beholding those great portents, hair-raising as they were, Khara laughed and addressed all the rākṣasas:

sanskrit: mahotpātān imān sarvān utthitān ghoradarśanān na cintayāmy ahaṃ vīryād balavān durbalān iva
english: "All these terrible great portents that have arisen—I heed them not. In my valor I am the strong one; I regard them as I would the weak."

sanskrit: tārā api śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ pātayeyaṃ nabhastalāt mṛtyuṃ maraṇadharmeṇa saṃkruddho yojayāmy aham
english: "Even the stars I could bring down from the vault of heaven with my sharp arrows. Enraged, I visit death upon all who are subject to death."

sanskrit: rāghavaṃ taṃ balotsiktaṃ bhrātaraṃ cāpi lakṣmaṇam ahatvā sāyakais tīkṣṇair nopāvartitum utsahe
english: "Without slaying that Rāghava—intoxicated with his strength—and his brother Lakṣmaṇa with my sharp arrows, I have no desire to turn back."

sanskrit: sakāmā bhaginī me 'stu pītvā tu rudhiraṃ tayoḥ yannimittaṃ tu rāmasya lakṣmaṇasya viparyayaḥ
english: "Let my sister have her desire fulfilled by drinking the blood of those two—for whose sake the destruction of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa has come about."

sanskrit: na kva cit prāptapūrvo me saṃyugeṣu parājayaḥ yuṣmākam etat pratyakṣaṃ nānṛtaṃ kathayāmy aham
english: "Never anywhere have I suffered defeat in battle—this is plain to you all; I speak no untruth."

sanskrit: devarājam api kruddho mattairāvatayāyinam vajrahastaṃ raṇe hanyāṃ kiṃ punas tau ca mānuṣau
english: "Enraged, I could slay even the king of the gods riding his intoxicated Airāvata with thunderbolt in hand—what then of these two mere mortals?"

sanskrit: sā tasya garjitaṃ śrutvā rākṣasasya mahācamūḥ praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe mṛtyupāśāvapāśitā
english: Hearing that rākṣasa's roar, the great army felt incomparable exultation—though it was already ensnared in the noose of death.

sanskrit: sameyuś ca mahātmāno yuddhadarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ ṛṣayo devagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca saha cāraṇaiḥ
english: And noble sages, gods, gandharvas, siddhas, and cāraṇas assembled, eager to witness the battle.

sanskrit: sametya coruḥ sahitās te 'nyāyaṃ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ svasti gobrāhmaṇebhyo 'stu lokānāṃ ye ca saṃmatāḥ
english: Gathering together, those of meritorious deeds spoke among themselves: "May there be welfare for the cows, the brāhmaṇas, and all beings held in esteem."

sanskrit: jayatāṃ rāghavo yuddhe paulastyān rajanīcarān cakrā hasto yathā yuddhe sarvān asurapuṃgavān
english: "May Rāghava be victorious in battle over the night-roaming descendants of Pulastya, just as Cakra-handed Indra was victorious over all the foremost asuras."

sanskrit: etac cānyac ca bahuśo bruvāṇāḥ paramarṣayaḥ dadṛśur vāhinīṃ teṣāṃ rākṣasānāṃ gatāyuṣām
english: Saying this and much else besides, the great seers beheld that army of rākṣasas whose lives were already spent.

sanskrit: rathena tu kharo vegāt sainyasyāgrād viniḥsṛtaḥ taṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ bhūyo rākṣasāś ca viniḥsṛtāḥ
english: Khara swiftly drove his chariot out ahead of the army; seeing that rākṣasa advance, the other rākṣasas also sallied forth.

sanskrit: śyena gāmī pṛthugrīvo yajñaśatrur vihaṃgamaḥ durjayaḥ karavīrākṣaḥ paruṣaḥ kālakārmukaḥ
english: Śyenagāmī, Pṛthugrīva, Yajñaśatru, Vihaṃgama, Durjaya, Karavīrākṣa, Paruṣa, and Kālakārmuka—

sanskrit: meghamālī mahāmālī sarpāsyo rudhirāśanaḥ dvādaśaite mahāvīryāḥ pratasthur abhitaḥ kharam
english: Meghamālī, Mahāmālī, Sarpāsya, and Rudhirāśana—these twelve of great valor set forth surrounding Khara on all sides.

sanskrit: mahākapālaḥ sthūlākṣaḥ pramāthī triśirās tathā catvāra ete senāgryā dūṣaṇaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayuḥ
english: And four foremost commanders—Mahākapāla, Sthūlākṣa, Pramāthī, and Triśiras—followed behind Dūṣaṇa.

sanskrit: sā bhīmavegā samarābhikāmā sudāruṇā rākṣasavīra senā tau rājaputrau sahasābhyupetā mālāgrahāṇām iva candrasūryau
english: That fearsome, battle-hungry, utterly terrible army of rākṣasa warriors suddenly descended upon those two princes as clouds descend upon the sun and moon at eclipse-time.

sanskrit: āśramaṃ prati yāte tu khare kharaparākrame tān evautpātikān rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā dadarśa ha
english: When Khara of fierce valor marched toward the hermitage, Rāma along with his brother witnessed those very portents.

sanskrit: tān utpātān mahāghorān utthitān romaharṣaṇān prajānām ahitān dṛṣṭvā vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Seeing those great and terrible portents arise—hair-raising and harmful to all creatures—he spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: imān paśya mahābāho sarvabhūtāpahāriṇaḥ samutthitān mahotpātān saṃhartuṃ sarvarākṣasān
english: "O mighty-armed one, behold these great portents that have arisen to sweep away all living beings—portending the destruction of all the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: amī rudhiradhārās tu visṛjantaḥ kharasvanān vyomni meghā vivartante paruṣā gardabhāruṇāḥ
english: "Those harsh, donkey-hued clouds rolling in the sky, raining down streams of blood and uttering braying sounds—"

sanskrit: sadhūmāś ca śarāḥ sarve mama yuddhābhinandinaḥ rukmapṛṣṭhāni cāpāni viveṣṭante ca lakṣmaṇa
english: "And all my arrows, Lakṣmaṇa—they who delight in battle—smoke; and my gold-backed bows tremble."

sanskrit: yādṛśā iha kūjanti pakṣiṇo vanacāriṇaḥ agrato no bhayaṃ prāptaṃ saṃśayo jīvitasya ca
english: "The manner in which these forest-roaming birds cry out here foretells that danger has come upon us and that our lives hang in uncertainty."

sanskrit: saṃprahāras tu sumahān bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ayam ākhyāti me bāhuḥ sphuramāṇo muhur muhuḥ
english: "A great clash of battle will surely occur—of this there is no doubt; this arm of mine, throbbing again and again, proclaims it."

sanskrit: saṃnikarṣe tu naḥ śūra jayaṃ śatroḥ parājayam suprabhaṃ ca prasannaṃ ca tava vaktraṃ hi lakṣyate
english: "O hero, your face appearing bright and serene at this juncture portends our victory and the enemy's defeat."

sanskrit: udyatānāṃ hi yuddhārthaṃ yeṣāṃ bhavati lakṣmaṇaḥ niṣprabhaṃ vadanaṃ teṣāṃ bhavaty āyuḥ parikṣayaḥ
english: "For those about to engage in battle whose faces, O Lakṣmaṇa, appear lustreless—their lives dwindle away."

sanskrit: anāgatavidhānaṃ tu kartavyaṃ śubham icchatā āpadaṃ śaṅkamānena puruṣeṇa vipaścitā
english: "One who desires good fortune and who suspects danger must make provision against what is yet to come—so must a wise man act."

sanskrit: tasmād gṛhītvā vaidehīṃ śarapāṇir dhanurdharaḥ guhām āśrayaśailasya durgāṃ pādapasaṃkulām
english: "Therefore, taking Vaidehī, bearing arrows in hand and bow strung, take shelter in the difficult cave of the mountain, dense with trees—"

sanskrit: pratikūlitum icchāmi na hi vākyam idaṃ tvayā śāpito mama pādābhyāṃ gamyatāṃ vatsa māciram
english: "I wish to encounter them head-on. Do not oppose this word of mine. By my feet I adjure you—go, my dear, and without delay."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ saha sītayā śarān ādāya cāpaṃ ca guhāṃ durgāṃ samāśrayat
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, taking his arrows and bow along with Sītā, took shelter in the difficult cave.

sanskrit: tasmin praviṣṭe tu guhāṃ lakṣmaṇe saha sītayā hanta niryuktam ity uktvā rāmaḥ kavacam āviśat
english: When Lakṣmaṇa had entered the cave together with Sītā, Rāma said "Good, the duty is assigned," and donned his armor.

sanskrit: sā tenāgninikāśena kavacena vibhūṣitaḥ babhūva rāmas timire vidhūmo 'gnir ivotthitaḥ
english: Adorned with that armor blazing like fire, Rāma appeared in the darkness like a smokeless fire leaping up.

sanskrit: sa cāpam udyamya mahac charān ādāya vīryavān babhūvāvasthitas tatra jyāsvanaiḥ pūrayan diśaḥ
english: The valiant one, raising his great bow and taking up his arrows, stood there filling all the directions with the twang of his bowstring.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca saha cāraṇaiḥ ūcuḥ paramasaṃtrastā guhyakāś ca parasparam
english: Then the gods along with gandharvas, siddhas, cāraṇas, and guhyakas, greatly alarmed, spoke among themselves:

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām ekaś ca rāmo dharmātmā kathaṃ yuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds—and Rāma alone, righteous of soul. How will this battle unfold?"

sanskrit: tato gambhīranirhrādaṃ ghoravarmāyudhadhvajam anīkaṃ yātudhānānāṃ samantāt pratyadṛśyata
english: Then the army of the yātudhānas appeared on all sides with deep reverberating sounds, with fearsome armor, weapons, and banners.

sanskrit: siṃhanādaṃ visṛjatām anyonyam abhigarjatām cāpāni vispharayatāṃ jṛmbhatāṃ cāpy abhīkṣṇaśaḥ
english: Uttering lion-roars, bellowing at one another, twanging their bows, and yawning again and again—

sanskrit: vipraghuṣṭasvanānāṃ ca dundubhīṃś cāpi nighnatām teṣāṃ sutumulaḥ śabdaḥ pūrayām āsa tad vanam
english: —and beating kettledrums with resounding noise, their tumultuous clamor filled that forest completely.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastāḥ śvāpadā vanacāriṇaḥ dudruvur yatra niḥśabdaṃ pṛṣṭhato nāvalokayan
english: Terrified by that sound, the beasts of prey roaming the forest fled to wherever it was silent, not looking back.

sanskrit: tat tv anīkaṃ mahāvegaṃ rāmaṃ samupasarpata ghṛtanānāpraharaṇaṃ gambhīraṃ sāgaropamam
english: That army of great momentum, holding various weapons aloft, deep and ocean-like, advanced toward Rāma.

sanskrit: rāmo 'pi cārayaṃś cakṣuḥ sarvato raṇapaṇḍitaḥ dadarśa kharasainyaṃ tad yuddhābhimukham udyatam
english: Rāma too, skilled in battle, casting his eyes in all directions, beheld Khara's army drawn up and advancing with battle intent.

sanskrit: vitatya ca dhanur bhīmaṃ tūṇyāś coddhṛtya sāyakān krodham āhārayat tīvraṃ vadhārthaṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: Drawing his terrible bow and pulling arrows from his quiver, he summoned fierce wrath for the slaughter of all the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: duṣprekṣyaḥ so 'bhavat kruddho yugāntāgnir iva jvalan taṃ dṛṣṭvā tejasāviṣṭaṃ prāvyathan vanadevatāḥ
english: Enraged, he became difficult to look upon, blazing like the fire at the end of an eon; seeing him possessed by that radiance, the forest deities trembled.

sanskrit: tasya kruddhasya rūpaṃ tu rāmasya dadṛśe tadā dakṣasyeva kratuṃ hantum udyatasya pinākinaḥ
english: The form of Rāma enraged was seen then as that of Piṇākin Śiva ready to strike down the sacrifice of Dakṣa.

sanskrit: avaṣṭabdhadhanuṃ rāmaṃ kruddhaṃ ca ripughātinam dadarśāśramam āgamya kharaḥ saha puraḥsaraiḥ
english: Khara, arriving at the hermitage along with his vanguard, beheld Rāma gripping his bow, enraged and the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā saguṇaṃ cāpam udyamya kharaniḥsvanam rāmasyābhimukhaṃ sūtaṃ codyatām ity acodayat
english: Seeing him, Khara raised his bow with its string in place, and roaring like a donkey, urged his charioteer: "Drive forward toward Rāma."

sanskrit: sa kharasyājñayā sūtas turagān samacodayat yatra rāmo mahābāhur eko dhunvan dhanuḥ sthitaḥ
english: At Khara's command the charioteer drove the horses toward where the mighty-armed Rāma stood alone, wielding his bow.

sanskrit: taṃ tu niṣpatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve te rajanīcarāḥ nardamānā mahānādaṃ sacivāś ca paryavārayan
english: Seeing him charge forward, all those night-roaming companions shouted with great cries and surrounded him.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ yātudhānānāṃ madhye rato gataḥ kharaḥ babhūva madhye tārāṇāṃ lohitāṅga ivoditaḥ
english: Khara, having plunged into the midst of those yātudhānas, appeared like the red-limbed Mars risen in the midst of stars.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ bhīmadhanvānaṃ kruddhāḥ sarve niśācarāḥ rāmaṃ nānāvidhaiḥ śastrair abhyavarṣanta durjayam
english: Then all those night-roamers, enraged, rained various weapons upon that invincible Rāma of the terrible bow.

sanskrit: mudgarair āyasaiḥ śūlaiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ rākṣasāḥ samare rāmaṃ nijaghnū roṣatatparāḥ
english: The rākṣasas, intent on fury, struck Rāma in battle with iron clubs, spears, javelins, swords, and battle-axes.

sanskrit: te balāhakasaṃkāśā mahānādā mahābalāḥ abhyadhāvanta kākutsthaṃ rāmaṃ yuddhe jighāṃsavaḥ
english: Those mighty ones, resembling storm-clouds, roaring loudly, charged at Kākutstha Rāma in battle, intent on killing him.

sanskrit: te rāme śaravarṣāṇi vyasṛjan rakṣasāṃ guṇāḥ śailendram iva dhārābhir varṣamāṇā mahādhanāḥ
english: Those mighty rākṣasas discharged showers of arrows upon Rāma, like great rainclouds drenching the king of mountains with their torrents.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto ghorai rāghavo rakṣasāṃ gaṇaiḥ tithiṣv iva mahādevo vṛtaḥ pāriṣadāṃ gaṇaiḥ
english: Surrounded by those terrible hosts of rākṣasas, Rāghava appeared like Mahādeva surrounded by his host of attendants on festival days.

sanskrit: tāni muktāni śastrāṇi yātudhānaiḥ sa rāghavaḥ pratijagrāha viśikhair nadyoghān iva sāgaraḥ
english: Those weapons hurled by the yātudhānas, Rāghava received with his own shafts, as the ocean receives the floods of rivers.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ praharaṇair ghorair bhinnagātro na vivyathe rāmaḥ pradīptair bahubhir vajrair iva mahācalaḥ
english: Though his body was pierced by those terrible weapons, Rāma did not waver—like a great mountain struck by many blazing thunderbolts.

sanskrit: sa viddhaḥ kṣatajādigdhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāghavaḥ babhūva rāmaḥ saṃdhyābhrair divākara ivāvṛtaḥ
english: Rāghava, pierced and drenched in blood over all his limbs, appeared like the sun enveloped by twilight clouds.

sanskrit: viṣedur devagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ ekaṃ sahastrair bahubhis tadā dṛṣṭvā samāvṛtam
english: The gods, gandharvas, siddhas, and great seers were filled with dismay seeing him—one man—surrounded by many thousands.

sanskrit: tato rāmaḥ susaṃkruddho maṇḍalīkṛtakārmukaḥ sasarja niśitān bāṇāñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Then Rāma, greatly enraged, drew his bow to a full circle and released sharp arrows by the hundreds and then thousands.

sanskrit: durāvārān durviṣahān kālapāśopamān raṇe mumoca līlayā rāmaḥ kaṅkapatrān ajihmagān
english: Rāma released with ease in battle those straight-flying, heron-feathered arrows—difficult to ward off, difficult to endure, resembling the noose of Time.

sanskrit: te śarāḥ śatrusainyeṣu muktā rāmeṇa līlayā ādadū rakṣasāṃ prāṇān pāśāḥ kālakṛtā iva
english: Those arrows released so effortlessly by Rāma into the enemy's army bore away the lives of the rākṣasas like the nooses fashioned by Time.

sanskrit: bhittvā rākṣasadehāṃs tāṃs te śarā rudhirāplutāḥ antarikṣagatā rejur dīptāgnisamatejasaḥ
english: Piercing through the bodies of the rākṣasas, those arrows, soaked in blood and blazing with the radiance of kindled fire, shone as they passed through the sky.

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyās tu rāmasya sāyakāś cāpamaṇḍalāt viniṣpetur atīvogrā rakṣaḥ prāṇāpahāriṇaḥ
english: Innumerable, exceedingly fierce arrows of Rāma—life-takers of rākṣasas—poured forth from the orb of his bow.

sanskrit: tair dhanūṃṣi dhvajāgrāṇi varmāṇi ca śirāṃsi ca bahūn sahastābharaṇān ūrūn karikaropamān
english: With those arrows he shattered bows, the tops of standards, and coats of armor; he struck off heads and the many thighs adorned with bracelets—thighs resembling elephant trunks.

sanskrit: tato nālīkanārācais tīkṣṇāgraiś ca vikarṇibhiḥ bhīmam ārtasvaraṃ cakrur bhidyamānā niśācarāḥ
english: Then, pierced by nālīka and nārāca arrows with their sharp points and by vikarṇi shafts, the night-roamers emitted terrible cries of anguish.

sanskrit: tat sainyaṃ niśitair bāṇair arditaṃ marmabhedibhiḥ rāmeṇa na sukhaṃ lebhe śuṣkaṃ vanam ivāgninā
english: That army, tormented by Rāma's sharp arrows that pierced the vital points, found no ease—like a dry forest in fire.

sanskrit: ke cid bhīmabalāḥ śūrāḥ śūlān khaḍgān paraśvadhān cikṣipuḥ paramakruddhā rāmāya rajanīcarāḥ
english: Some of the night-roaming heroes of tremendous strength, exceedingly enraged, hurled spears, swords, and battle-axes at Rāma.

sanskrit: tāni bāṇair mahābāhuḥ śastrāṇy āvārya rāghavaḥ jahāra samare prāṇāṃś ciccheda ca śirodharān
english: The mighty-armed Rāghava, intercepting those weapons with his arrows, robbed them of their lives in battle and severed their necks.

sanskrit: avaśiṣṭāś ca ye tatra viṣaṇṇāś ca niśācarāḥ kharam evābhyadhāvanta śaraṇārthaṃ śarārditāḥ
english: And the night-roamers who remained there, despondent and tormented by arrows, fled toward Khara himself seeking refuge.

sanskrit: tān sarvān punar ādāya samāśvāsya ca dūṣaṇaḥ abhyadhāvata kākutsthaṃ kruddho rudram ivāntakaḥ
english: Dūṣaṇa, taking all of them back and reassuring them, charged at Kākutstha—enraged as Yama before Rudra.

sanskrit: nivṛttās tu punaḥ sarve dūṣaṇāśrayanirbhayāḥ rāmam evābhyadhāvanta sālatālaśilāyudhāḥ
english: All of them, having turned back and now fearless under Dūṣaṇa's shelter, once more charged at Rāma, armed with śāla trees, palmyra palms, and rocks.

sanskrit: tad babhūvādbhutaṃ yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ romaharṣaṇam rāmasyāsya mahāghoraṃ punas teṣāṃ ca rakṣasām
english: That battle—between Rāma and those rākṣasas—became wondrous, tumultuous, hair-raising, and supremely terrible.
